title: Duties 7–9: oral health, reflection & well-being
blurb: Promoting oral health to patients and communities, reflecting on and developing your practice, and looking after your own and your team's well-being.
question: The assessor asks: "How do you promote oral health, how do you learn from your experiences, and how do you look after yourself at work?" What would a strong, evidence-based answer to each part include?

teach.h: Three duties about health and growth
teach.body: Duty 7 is to promote oral health to individuals and the wider population, and raise awareness of its role in preventing ill health in communities. Duty 8 is to reflect on, review and develop the quality of your own practice. Duty 9 is to manage your own health and well-being and promote the well-being of others in the team. One looks outward at patients and communities, one looks at your practice, and one looks after you and your colleagues.

teach.h: Duty 7: advice that is evidence-based and personal
teach.body: Oral health advice should follow Delivering Better Oral Health (4th edition) and be tailored to the person, so it is realistic and motivating rather than a lecture. Dental nurses advise, support and motivate patients to prevent disease. Duty 7 also looks wider: oral health inequalities, community programmes in schools or care homes, and links between oral and general health, such as sugar, smoking and alcohol.

head: Who
Advice
rows: Smear of toothpaste, at least 1,000 ppm fluoride
Pea-sized amount, at least 1,000 ppm fluoride
Cut down how often sugary food and drinks are taken
teach.caption: Children giving cause for concern may be advised to use 1,350–1,500 ppm from younger ages. Higher-strength toothpastes are prescribed by the dentist.

teach.body: Insight is understanding your own strengths, limits, assumptions and how your actions affect others. It matters because a nurse who knows the edge of their competence asks for help before patients are put at risk. Reflection is how insight grows: you look back at an experience, work out what it means, and decide what to do differently. Reflective models give that thinking a structure so it leads to learning, not just a description.

teach.caption: What happened? What did you think and feel? What went well or badly? Why? What could you have done differently? What will you do next time?

teach.h: GDC Enhanced CPD for dental nurses

items.label: at least, in every 2 consecutive CPD years
a personal development plan is required
annual CPD statement to the GDC

teach.caption: Recommended topics include medical emergencies (at least 10 h per cycle), decontamination (5 h) and radiography (5 h, if you take radiographs).

teach.body: Personal development planning means identifying what you need to learn (from feedback, appraisal, reflection and your scope), planning how, then recording the evidence and reflecting on what changed. Every verifiable CPD activity links to a GDC development outcome: A communication, B management and leadership, C knowledge and skills, or D behaviours that maintain patient confidence. This cycle is how you keep your knowledge and competence up to date throughout your career.

teach.h: Duty 9: looking after yourself and the team
teach.body: Dental nursing is busy, physical and sometimes emotionally hard. Duty 9 asks you to notice your own warning signs, use healthy coping strategies (reflection, self-acceptance, debriefing, peer support, handing over to a colleague and asking for help), and manage your time and workload. If your health or well-being starts to affect your work or relationships, you act on it and seek advice. You also look out for colleagues.

steps.label: Use support
steps.sub: Occupational health, GP, practice wellbeing support

steps.label: Review
steps.sub: Is it improving? Keep checking in

teach.caption: If your health could affect patient safety, seek advice and adapt how you work. Asking for help is a professional strength.

teach.text: A reflection that only describes what happened shows no learning. Description is just the first stage. The value is in the analysis (why it happened) and the action plan (what you'll do differently), so make sure your examples reach the end of the cycle.

items: Duty 7: evidence-based, tailored oral health advice (DBOH 4th edn), plus community and inequalities.
Duty 8: insight and reflection; use a model such as Gibbs to reach an action plan.
Enhanced CPD: 50 h per 5 years, at least 10 h every 2 years, PDP, annual statement.
Duty 9: self-monitor, cope healthily, manage workload, seek help, support colleagues.
Act if your well-being starts to affect your work or patient safety.

summary: You can now give evidence-based oral health advice in line with Delivering Better Oral Health, explain insight and use Gibbs' cycle to reflect, state the GDC's Enhanced CPD requirements, and describe how you protect your own and your team's well-being, ready to evidence duties 7, 8 and 9.

A.q: A parent asks how much toothpaste to use for her 2-year-old. What does Delivering Better Oral Health advise?
options: A pea-sized amount of 1,450 ppm toothpaste
No toothpaste at all until every baby tooth is through
A smear of toothpaste with at least 1,000 ppm fluoride
A full brush-length of children's low-fluoride paste
A.why: For children under 3, DBOH advises a smear of toothpaste containing at least 1,000 ppm fluoride.

whyNot.0: A pea-sized amount is advised from age 3.
whyNot.1: Brushing with fluoride toothpaste should start as soon as the first tooth appears.
whyNot.3: A full brush-length is too much, and low-fluoride paste is not what DBOH recommends.

A.q: In Gibbs' reflective cycle, which stage comes straight after "Feelings"?
options: Action plan
Evaluation
Conclusion
Description
A.why: Gibbs' order is Description, Feelings, Evaluation, Analysis, Conclusion, Action plan.

whyNot.0: The action plan is the final stage.
whyNot.2: Conclusion comes after Evaluation and Analysis.
whyNot.3: Description is the first stage, before Feelings.

A.q: How much verifiable CPD must a dental nurse complete in each 5-year cycle?
options: 10 hours
25 hours
75 hours
50 hours
A.why: Dental nurses need 50 hours of verifiable CPD per 5-year cycle, with at least 10 hours in every two consecutive years.

whyNot.0: 10 hours is the minimum in every two-year period, not the cycle total.
whyNot.1: 25 hours is not the GDC requirement for dental nurses.
whyNot.2: 75 hours is more than the GDC asks of dental nurses; their figure is 50.

B.q: Which is the best description of "insight" in professional practice?
options: Understanding your own abilities, limits and impact on others
Being able to predict which patients will need treatment next
Knowing every clinical guideline off by heart
Having the most years of experience in the team
B.why: Insight means understanding your strengths, limitations and assumptions and how your behaviour affects others, which keeps patients safe.

whyNot.1: Predicting treatment needs is clinical judgement, and diagnosis is the dentist's role.
whyNot.2: Knowing guidelines is knowledge, not insight into yourself.

B.q: After a difficult medical emergency in the surgery, a colleague is visibly shaken. Which response best fits duty 9?
options: Tell her to put it behind her and see the next patient
Suggest a team debrief and check how she is feeling
Avoid mentioning it so she doesn't get more upset
Report her to the manager for being unprofessional
B.why: Debriefing and peer support are recognised coping strategies, and duty 9 includes promoting the well-being of others in the team.

whyNot.0: Ignoring distress can harm well-being and safety.
whyNot.2: Avoiding the subject leaves her unsupported.
whyNot.3: Being upset after an emergency is a normal reaction, not unprofessional behaviour.

B.q: Which toothpaste advice does DBOH give for adults?
options: At least 1,000 ppm fluoride, then rinse well with water
5,000 ppm fluoride toothpaste for every adult patient
Fluoride-free toothpaste twice a day to protect enamel
1,350–1,500 ppm fluoride twice daily, spit, don't rinse
B.why: Adults should brush twice daily with 1,350–1,500 ppm fluoride toothpaste and spit, not rinse, so fluoride stays on the teeth.

whyNot.0: Rinsing washes fluoride away, and adults should use 1,350–1,500 ppm.
whyNot.1: 5,000 ppm is prescribed by a dentist for adults at higher risk, not for everyone.
whyNot.2: Fluoride toothpaste is the key preventive measure.

C.q: Which of these is NOT part of the GDC's Enhanced CPD requirements for dental nurses?
options: Keeping a personal development plan
Making an annual CPD statement to the GDC
Sitting a yearly NEBDN refresher exam
Linking CPD to development outcomes
C.why: There is no yearly NEBDN exam. Enhanced CPD requires a PDP, an annual statement, and verifiable CPD linked to development outcomes.

whyNot.1: An annual CPD statement is required.
whyNot.3: Each verifiable CPD activity must link to at least one development outcome.

C.q: After weeks of extra shifts you feel exhausted and have made two small errors. What is the best action?
options: Speak to your manager and seek support
Keep going until the busy period ends
Take energy drinks to get through clinics
Hide the errors so you don't worry anyone
C.why: Duty 9 means recognising when well-being is affecting your work and acting, such as talking to your manager, adjusting workload and seeking advice.

whyNot.1: Pushing on while making errors puts patients and you at risk.
whyNot.2: This masks the problem without addressing it.
whyNot.3: Hiding errors breaches candour and leaves risks unaddressed.

C.q: Which is an example of promoting oral health at community level rather than to one patient?
options: Giving brushing advice to a patient in the chair
Showing one patient how to use interdental brushes properly
Recording a patient's diet history at a routine check-up
Supporting a supervised toothbrushing scheme in nurseries
C.why: Supervised toothbrushing schemes reach many children at once, which is a community, population-level approach.

whyNot.0: Chairside advice is individual oral health promotion.
whyNot.1: One-to-one instruction is individual, not community level.
whyNot.2: A diet history supports one patient's prevention plan.

reteach.title: A window, a mirror and a fuel gauge
reteach.question: If duties 7, 8 and 9 were three things on your dashboard, what would each one show you?

blocks.body: Duty 7 is a window: you look out at your patients and community and help them stay healthy. Duty 8 is a mirror: you look honestly at your own practice, see what went well and what didn't, and plan to improve. Duty 9 is a fuel gauge: you keep an eye on your own reserves, and your team's, and refuel before you run empty. A safe nurse checks all three regularly.

head: Tool
Duty
Ask yourself
rows: Is my advice evidence-based and personal?
What did I learn and what will I change?
Am I, and my team, coping?

blocks.text: Looking in the mirror isn't the same as criticising yourself. Reflection includes what went well and builds self-acceptance, which is one of the coping strategies in duty 9.

explain.body: Use Delivering Better Oral Health and tailor it. Advise, support and motivate individuals, and support community approaches that reduce inequalities.

test.q: Why do we advise patients to spit, not rinse, after brushing?
options: To save water at the sink
To stop the toothpaste foaming too much
To keep fluoride on the teeth for longer
To avoid swallowing loose brush bristles
test.why: Not rinsing leaves fluoride on the tooth surface, increasing its protective effect.

whyNot.0: Saving water isn't the reason for the advice.
whyNot.1: Foaming is unrelated to rinsing advice.
whyNot.3: Bristles aren't swallowed in normal brushing; the point is fluoride contact.

explain.body: Insight is knowing your strengths, limits and impact. Gibbs' cycle structures reflection: Description, Feelings, Evaluation, Analysis, Conclusion, Action plan.

test.q: Which stage of Gibbs' cycle asks "Why did it happen that way?"
options: Analysis
Description
Feelings
Action plan
test.why: Analysis is where you make sense of the situation and explore why things happened.

whyNot.2: Feelings covers what you thought and felt.
whyNot.3: The action plan sets out what you'll do next time.

explain.body: 50 hours of verifiable CPD per 5-year cycle, at least 10 hours in every 2 consecutive years, a PDP, an annual statement, and every activity linked to a development outcome (A to D).

test.q: Which GDC development outcome covers management of self and others, teamwork and leadership?
options: Outcome A
Outcome C
Outcome D
Outcome B
test.why: Outcome B covers management of self and others, teamwork and leadership.

whyNot.1: Outcome C is knowledge and skills in your field.
whyNot.2: Outcome D is behaviours that maintain patient confidence.

explain.body: Self-monitor, use healthy coping strategies, manage time and workload, ask for help, and look out for colleagues. Act if well-being affects your work.

test.q: Which is a healthy coping strategy named in the dental nurse standard?
options: Working through every lunch break to catch up
Handing over to a colleague when needed
Avoiding feedback from the team
Keeping worries to yourself
test.why: Handing over to a colleague, along with debriefing, peer support and asking for help, is a recognised coping strategy.

whyNot.0: Skipping breaks increases fatigue and risk.
whyNot.3: Bottling up worries isn't a healthy strategy.
